newsitem.title: USA: Boeing estimates raised by Merrill Lynch.
newsitem.headline: Boeing estimates raised by Merrill Lynch.

text.p: Merrill Lynch raised its earnings estimates for Boeing Co based on savings expected from the company's decision to withdraw plans to build a stretch version of its 747 jet, analyst Byron Callan said.
Callan said the brokerage raised its 1997 earnings estimate to $6.45 a share from $6.00 on a pro-forma basis, assuming completion of the company's planned acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp.
For 1998 the brokerage raised its estimate to $8.00 a share from $7.20, and for 1999 the estimate was raised to $8.60 from $7.70.

For 2000 the brokerage raised its estimate to $10.75 a share from $9.70, Callan said. He said the decision could cut annual research and development costs by as much as $500 million annually over the next five years.
